description: Eighty-eight inches of flat glass in a brushed-chrome bezel, wall-hung facing the platform bed, thinner than a knife and wider than the bed it faces. None of the fishbowl bulge, none of the phosphor lines, none of the slow salvaged-CRT wobble everyone else watches the world through — the picture simply sits there, corner to corner, and stays put. CHROMAVISION is etched across the bottom rail in a typeface that was somebody's idea of the future, over a row of touch keys that come up amber when the set wakes. Polaris built it for people who wanted the wall to be the screen and were in a position to ask.
name: Polaris Executive Chromavision 88
